candidates.name: hospitality-alt-data-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit research tool building a near-real-time US lodging-demand proxy for MAR/HLT/H between earnings prints, from entirely free/keyless public sources: TSA checkpoint throughput (2019+), Google Trends brand search (pytrends, 6 hotel brands), BLS employment/JOLTS/PPI for traveler accommodation, yfinance prices/earnings dates, plus one committed hand-keyed file `data/reported_revpar.csv` (quarterly RevPAR for MAR/HLT/H with source URLs — same underlying idea as our 'MAR/HLT RevPAR from releases' but committed as a clean CSV with source links). README states explicitly this is a RevPAR *proxy*, not real STR data ("True RevPAR is STR data (paid)"), substituting BLS accommodation employment/PPI as demand/rate proxies. Reports its own honest backtest: deseasonalized MoM r≈0.41 (p≈0.003) vs RevPAR, but a composite TSA+brand-search+JOLTS signal fails out of sample (r=-0.14 steady state, p≈0.09 on a trading overlay). 32 commits, CI runs daily to refresh data and publish outputs as GitHub Actions artifacts; no paid keys required (optional BLS_API_KEY for higher limits).
candidates.why_useful: Directly on gap #8 (hotel supply/demand STR/CoStar proxy) and gap #17 (nowcasting method transparency). Even though it is explicitly a proxy rather than licensed STR data, it is a working, keyless, one-command pull architecture (TSA+BLS+PPI+Trends+yfinance) we could fork or mine for the BLS accommodation-employment/PPI series we may not already be pulling, and its self-reported failure of the composite signal is a useful negative data point consistent with our own TSA/Trends null results.
candidates.size_hint: small hand-keyed CSV + gitignored cached pulls; 32 commits
candidates.last_activity: not confirmed in fetch (active enough to run daily CI as of check)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps our existing 'MAR/HLT RevPAR from releases' and our own tested-and-failed TSA-throughput / Google-Trends constructions — still worth flagging for the BLS PPI/accommodation-employment proxy angle we may not have tried, and as a second working example of the same null result on TSA/Trends.

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (everythingscraper)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client wrapping an Apify Actor that returns "STR analytics on tap": occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, and 12-month calendars, computed directly from live Airbnb listing pages (not Inside Airbnb dumps). No data committed to the repo itself — it is a paid-Apify-actor client, so use requires an Apify subscription and scrapes airbnb.com directly.
candidates.why_useful: If it works as advertised it would give realised ADR/occupancy/RevPAR at the listing level for STRs (our gap #2), which none of our current sources provide. But it scrapes airbnb.com directly, which our repo rules classify as a ToS decision for a human, not something to run — catalogued as method only, left unrun.

candidates.name: Africa Mauritius Hotel Room Occupancy Rate datasets (electricsheepafrica)
candidates.what_it_holds: Five small Hugging Face dataset cards from the electricsheepafrica org (part of a larger pan-African open-statistics project): 'Africa Mauritius Hotel Room Occupancy Rate' at all-hotels and large-hotels granularity, and quarterly/monthly cuts, ~10-60 rows each, sourced from Mauritius national statistics, updated Aug 2026, covering roughly 2019-2023. No linked GitHub pipeline repo could be confirmed from the org page.
candidates.why_useful: Genuine, government-sourced hotel occupancy time series (not synthetic/Kaggle), which is rare to find at all on open platforms — but it is Mauritius only, a market irrelevant to ABNB's segment mix, and very short/low-frequency. Cataloguing as a proof that national-statistics-office hotel occupancy series do get mirrored onto HF/GitHub by these scraping projects; worth a look for whether the same org/pipeline covers a bigger STR-relevant country (not confirmed).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Distinct from our Hawaii DBEDT series (different country) but same category (national hotel-occupancy statistics office data)

notes: This theme yielded thin results and the run was materially hampered: the session's WebSearch quota (200 calls, shared across all concurrent scout subagents) was already exhausted before this scout's first query, so all WebSearch calls failed outright; github.com/search was also 429 rate-limited (again, shared load from other scouts hitting GitHub). Work was done entirely via WebFetch against github.com/topics/* pages (which worked reliably), Bing/DuckDuckGo search-result pages fetched via WebFetch (Bing returned generic/no results for site:github.com queries — likely because WebFetch's summarizer received a JS-rendered or blocked page rather than raw SERPs; DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint hit a CAPTCHA wall), and Hugging Face datasets search. Substantively: real, non-proprietary STR/CoStar-equivalent hotel RevPAR/occupancy data is genuinely scarce on GitHub — STR and CoStar data is paid and litigiously protected, so almost everything indexed under hotel/RevPAR/occupancy topics on GitHub is either (a) synthetic/Kaggle-derived BI-dashboard portfolio projects (AtliQ Grands, Gujarat hotels, 119k-booking Kaggle set, etc. — excluded per instructions) or (b) commercial-real-estate scrapers unrelated to hotels that merely share the 'costar' keyword (CoStar Group also owns LoopNet/commercial real estate, causing false-positive topic hits). The one genuinely useful find (david984-code/hospitality-alt-data-dashboard) is itself explicit that true STR RevPAR is paid-only and that its free proxies (TSA, BLS PPI/employment, Google Trends) are weak — consistent with our own already-tested-and-failed TSA/Trends constructions. Recommend a follow-up scout with a working (non-rate-limited) `gh search code`/`gh search repos` pass once GitHub rate limits reset, specifically for terms 'HotStats', 'Kalibri Labs', 'STR SHARE Center', and 'hotel news now' scrapers, which this web-only pass could not reach cleanly.
